observations: Multiple white Intermediate Bulk Containers (IBC) in metal cages on wooden and plastic pallets.
Large black vertical plastic water tanks in the background.
The foreground IBC tank has a black top lid and a bottom discharge valve.
The metal cage of the foreground tank appears slightly bent at the bottom right.
The plastic inner containers appear translucent white.
The setting is an outdoor yard with a dirt floor.

claims.evidence: Requires a photo of the 'fork and glass' symbol or specific manufacturer stamping on the plastic bottle.

claims.claim: Used only once for clean water
claims.evidence: Previous contents cannot be determined by visual inspection of an empty tank.
Requires a photo of the tank filled with liquid or a close-up of the bottom valve area.
The top lid is visible on the foreground unit in photo 0.

risks.proof: Photo of the original manufacturer's label or the embossed food-grade symbol on the plastic.
Video of the valve handle turning and water flowing/stopping.

risks.risk: Structural damage to the cage or pallet
risks.proof: Photos of all four sides of the metal cage and the base pallet.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of any embossed symbols or text on the plastic tank to verify food-grade status.
Photo of the manufacturer's identification plate usually found on the metal cage.
Close-up photo of the bottom discharge valve.
Photo of the original labels if any remain on the tank.
response.reason: The items are clearly identifiable as standard 1000-liter IBC tanks. While the 'food grade' claim is unproven, they can be priced as used industrial containers in their current seen condition.
